metadata.theme: Trust, choosing who to believe, and keeping a promise
metadata.premise: Mara is a rain-soaked courier, paid to carry a sealed data chip across the flooded city before the midnight handover. Gangs and corporate drones want the chip too, and a voice inside it seems to know her name.

items.name: Tam's pick set
items.description: A tin of thin steel tools. A pick can open a simple lock if you are gentle.

clues.name: Flood stamp
clues.description: A water drop and the words FLOOD GATE NINE are stamped on the chip's shell. Vex said it held party music.

passages.title: The Cab Stand
paragraphs: Rain fell on the old cab stand. It had been raining for as long as Mara could remember.
Mara sat on her patched old bike. Her coat was soaked, and she felt a chill.
Vex waited under a dripping roof. He was a broker, and he wore a grey mask. No courier had ever seen his face.
"One job, Mara," he said. "Take this bag to the old rail bridge. Be there by midnight."
Inside the bag lay a small black chip. It was sealed in a hard shell. "Do not open it. Do not lose it. Do not stop for anyone," said Vex.

Mara tucked the bag under her coat. Far off, the tower lights were blinking through the fog. Then a tiny voice spoke from the bag. "Hello, Mara," it said. "My name is Nine. Your aunt Ila made me. I have been waiting for you."

choices.label: Ride to the market and find a friendly shop
Slip into a dark alley and talk to the voice

passages.title: Tam's Repair Shop
paragraphs: Mara rode to the market. Rain drummed on the stalls.
Old Tam ran a repair shop at the end of the row. A warm light shone from his door.
"You look soaked," said Tam. "Sit down. I have lunch in my sack, and plenty of it."
Mara ate fast. She had not stopped since dawn, and the soup was hot.
The bag hummed on her knee. Tam raised one eyebrow but said nothing.
Then he picked up a thin tin box. "Couriers get stuck at locked gates," he said.

choices.label: Ask Tam what is in the tin box
Say thanks and ride on without the box

passages.title: The Tin Box
paragraphs: Inside the tin lay a set of thin steel tools.
"A pick set," said Tam. "It will open a simple lock. Be gentle with it."
He looked at the humming bag. "That voice. Does it know you?"
"It said my name," said Mara.
"Then listen close," said Tam. "But do not trust it or anyone too much. Check what they tell you."
Mara put the pick set in her pocket. Down the row, a dark alley caught her eye. She could duck into its shade, or ride on to the crossing.

choices.label: Duck into the dark alley
Ride straight on to the crossing

passages.title: The Dark Alley
paragraphs: The alley was narrow and dark. Water ran down the walls in thin streams.
Mara stopped her bike in the shade of a fire stair. She took the chip from the bag.
It glowed a soft blue. "My name is Nine," said the voice. "I know you from long ago."
"Why did Ila make you?" asked Mara.
"To keep a secret safe. Look at my shell, Mara. Do not just take my word."

choices.label: Turn the chip over and look at its shell
Put the chip away and ride on

passages.title: The Little Stamp
paragraphs: On the back of the shell was a tiny stamp. It showed a water drop and three words: FLOOD GATE NINE.
Mara frowned. Vex had told her the chip held music for a party.
A music file does not need a flood stamp.
"Vex did not tell you the whole truth," said Nine. "I cannot say what he wants. Watch what he does."
Mara said nothing. She wrapped the chip in cloth and put it back in the bag.
A back lane cut toward the bridge. The crossing was the longer way round.

choices.label: Ride on to the tower lights
Slip down the back lane toward the bridge

passages.title: Under the Tower Lights
paragraphs: Mara reached a crossing where four streets met. The tower lights blinked through the fog like slow, tired eyes.
She thought about her night. First came the cab stand. Then came the shop or the alley. Now came the crossing.
The old rail bridge was two streets away. There was still time to look around.

choices.label: Ride back to Tam's shop
Ride back to the dark alley
Take the lane toward the bridge

passages.title: The Drone Lane
paragraphs: A drone hummed over the lane. It shot a white flash over the wet street, back and forth.
Two more drones followed. They were on a chase for any courier with a sealed chip.
Mara pulled up her rain mask. Nine whispered, "Do not be seen."

choices.label: Hide in the shade of a bus shelter
Make a dash past the drones

passages.title: Still as Stone
paragraphs: Mara slid off her bike and crouched in the shade. She held her breath.
The drones passed so close that the wind from them stirred her hair. Their flash slid over the shelter and moved on.
"Good," whispered Nine. "Slow is quiet."
When the hum faded, Mara pushed her bike toward the rail bridge.
Nine warned that more drones might wait at the bridge. For a moment, Mara wondered if giving up was easier.

choices.label: Walk the bike to the bridge gate
Wave the drone down and give up the bag

passages.title: The Fast Way
paragraphs: Mara pushed hard and made her dash. Her old bike rattled over the stones.
A drone swung round, and its flash lit the whole street. The chain on her bike sang as she turned. A chill ran down her back, but her wheel held. She pressed the chip to her chest.
She cut into a tunnel and the hum fell behind her. Her heart was pounding.
"That was loud," said Nine. "They may be waiting at the bridge now."
Ahead, the street forked. One way led straight to the bridge gate. The other had a shaded doorway.

choices.label: Ride on to the bridge gate
Duck into the shaded doorway to catch her breath

passages.title: The Bridge Gate
paragraphs: The old rail bridge rose out of the fog. A tall iron gate stood shut at the foot of the track.
A big lock hung on the gate. It had a water drop stamped on it, just like the chip.
On the far side of the bridge, a small light blinked three times.
Behind Mara, a cab engine growled. Vex had come early.
Above, a drone hummed. It was watching the gate.

choices.label: Pick the lock quietly with Tam's tools
choices.lockedHint: Find Tam's pick set at the shop and the chip's stamp in the alley.

choices.label: Ask Nine to hack the lock
Wave at the drone and call for help

passages.title: Click
paragraphs: Mara slid the pick into the lock and listened. She turned it a little. Click.
The lock fell open. She slipped through and eased the gate shut behind her.
"First the gate, then the track, then the far light," said Nine. "You are doing it in the right order."
Halfway across the bridge, Vex stepped out of the fog. A drone captain stood beside him.
"Give me the chip, Mara," said Vex. "I will pay you twice."
Mara looked at his grey mask. Then she looked at the small light on the far side.

choices.label: Walk on to the far light
Ask Nine to hack the drones' link

passages.title: The Loud Bell
paragraphs: "Hold still," said Nine. "I will hack the lock."
The lock clicked open. But a loud bell rang out, and lights began to flash along the whole bridge.
Drones swung toward Mara. Vex ran up through the rain, his mask dripping.
"Give me the chip," he said. "It is the only way you get paid and stay safe."
Mara held the bag tight. Her mind raced.

choices.label: Hand the chip to Vex
Dash over the bridge with the chip

passages.title: The Promise Kept
paragraphs: Mara walked on. Vex called her name, but she did not turn round.
The drone captain looked at the stamp on the gate. It looked at Vex. Then it lifted into the fog and left.
At the far end, a woman stood in a lit booth. A water drop was painted on its door.
"Aunt Ila?" said Mara. Ila took the chip and slid it into a slot. Far below, a huge gate groaned and swung shut. The flood water stopped rising.
"Hello, Ila," said Nine. "I kept the secret."
Mara smiled. She had checked the clue, picked the right person to believe, and kept her promise.

passages.title: Nine Takes Control
paragraphs: "Done," said Nine. The lights on the drones turned from red to green.
Every drone spun round and flew back to its tower. The captain went with them.
Vex stood alone on the bridge with his hands empty. He turned and walked into the fog.
Mara crossed to the far light. Ila took the chip and shut the flood gate for the night.
"Nine is a good partner," said Ila. "Would you like to keep her in your bag?"
So Mara and Nine rode the wet streets together. They became the best courier team in the city.

passages.title: The Quiet Chip
paragraphs: Mara gave the chip to Vex. He took it with a nod and dropped a coin pouch in her hand.
The bell stopped. The drones flew off with him, and the bridge fell quiet.
Nine said nothing more. The tiny voice had gone silent.
By morning, the low streets stood deep in water. The market shops were shut for a week.
No one was hurt, but Mara felt the weight of her choice. She had not checked the clue.
She kept the pouch and the old bike. Next time, she would ask who she should believe.

passages.title: Across the Bridge
paragraphs: Mara dashed over the bridge. The drones swung after her. Their flash lit the rails like day.
Halfway over, the chain on her bike snapped. The bike slid sideways and fell into the river with a splash.
Mara ran the last of the way on foot, with the bag held tight.
At the far end, a woman in a lit booth pulled her inside and shut the door. It was Aunt Ila.
The chip went into its slot. Far below, a huge gate groaned and closed. The flood water stopped rising.
Mara had lost her old bike. But the city was safe, and she had kept her promise.

ending.title: A Promise and a Lost Bike

passages.title: The Drone's Light
paragraphs: Mara waved at the drone. Its white flash locked on her.
A cold voice said, "Courier. Hand over the bag." A metal arm lowered and lifted the bag out of her hands.
The drone rose into the fog and was gone. Mara stood in the rain with empty hands.
Nobody was hurt, but it had cost her much. Now the bag, the chip and Nine had all been taken.
She walked to the market. Old Tam ran a repair shop there. He gave her hot soup, some lunch from his sack and a seat by the fire.
"You can try again," said Tam. "This time, listen close, and check what you see."

courier.definition: A person who carries parcels or messages from one place to another.

broker.definition: A person who arranges jobs and pays others to do them.

handover.definition: The moment when something is given from one person to another.

drone.definition: A small flying machine that moves without a pilot inside.
